title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 174 (Pawnee not to retain for debt or promise other than that for which goods pledged)

content.overview: Section 174 provides that the pawnee shall not, in the absence of a contract to that effect, retain the goods pledged for any debt or promise other than the debt or promise for which they are pledged; but such contract, in the absence of anything to the contrary, shall be presumed in regard to subsequent advances made by the pawnee.
content.glance: Pawnee cannot retain for other debts or promises absent a contract to that effect; a contract is presumed for subsequent advances unless contrary intention appears.
content.study: The pawnee shall not, in the absence of a contract to that effect, retain the goods pledged for any debt or promise other than the debt or promise for which they are pledged; but such contract, in the absence of anything to the contrary, shall be presumed in regard to subsequent advances made by the pawnee. Current-law framing: general rule against retention for other obligations, with a presumption for subsequent advances.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The pawnee shall not, in the absence of a contract to that effect, retain the goods pledged for any debt or promise other than the debt or promise for which they are pledged; but such contract, in the absence of anything to the contrary, shall be presumed in regard to subsequent advances made by the pawnee.

examples.title: Subsequent advances
examples.body: Absent anything to the contrary, a contract to retain for subsequent advances by the pawnee is presumed under Section 174.

hypotheticals.question: May the pawnee retain the goods for a different debt absent an express contract?
hypotheticals.analysis: No, under Section 174, unless a contract to that effect exists. For subsequent advances a contract is presumed absent contrary intention.
